texts.preamble: Devaraj K S vs Marulasiddeshwara R J on 31 March, 2022 Author: Pradeep Singh Yerur Bench: Pradeep Singh Yerur -1- In The High Court Of Karnataka At Bengaluru Dated This The 31St Day Of March, 2022 Before The Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Pradeep Singh Yerur Miscellaneous First Appeal No.8953 Of 2019 (Mv-I) Between: Devaraj K.S. S/O.Kalachari Aged About 24 Years Vishwakarma Caste B.Sc. Graduate R/At Edehally Village Kasaba Hobli Holalkere - 577 526 ... Appellant (By Sri R.Shashidhara , Advocate) And: 1. Marulasiddeshwara R.J. S/O.Jayappa R.M. Major Prop:Shiva Transport Bearing Reg.No.Ka-16/B-3015 R/At Balaraj Urus Road Shivamogga - 577 201 2.
texts.facts: This appeal is preferred by the claimant challenging the judgment and award passed by Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Holalkere (for short 'the tribunal') in MVC.No.562/2017 dated 16.05.2019. This appeal is founded on the premise of inadequacy of compensation. 3. Parties to the appeal shall be referred to as per their status before the tribunal. 4. Brief facts of the case is as under: On 14.09.2015 at 10.15 a.m., when the claimant and his uncle were going towards main circle at Holalkere town by walking on the left side of the road, at that time, a bus bearing registration No.KA-16/B-3015 came with high speed in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and safety, dashed against the claimant from behind, thereby causing accident resulting in grievous injuries being sustained by the claimant, immediately after the accident, the claimant was taken to Government Hospital, Holalkere where he took initial treatment and on the basis of advice of Doctor, he was shifted to Davanagere Private Hospital and thereafter shifted to Chitradurga Private Hospital for further treatment and despite having taken treatment in three hospitals, he is still undergoing further treatment. It is also stated by the claimant that he has expended huge amount of money for his treatment and due to the fracture suffered, as a result of the accident, his future earning capacity is diminished. Hence, he has filed a claim petition before the tribunal seeking compensation. 4.1. On service of notice, respondents appeared before the tribunal and filed their separate statement of objections denying the claim made by the claimant. Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107752679/ 2 Respondent No.1 took up the plea that the claim petition is not maintainable and also stated that he is not liable to pay the compensation where as respondent No.2 denied entire claim petition inter alia contending that the accident occurred due to the fault of claimant while he was suddenly crossing the road without observing traffic rules. Respondent No.2 has also taken the plea that the documents produced by the claimant are all fabricated and concocted and hence, it is not liable to pay any compensation. It is also pleaded by respondent No.2 that the driver of the alleged bus had no valid licence to drive class of vehicle as on the date of occurrence of accident. Hence, on this ground, he has sought for dismissal of claim petition. 4.2. The tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration on the basis of pleadings of the parties. 4.3. In order to substantiate the issues and to establish his case, the claimant got himself examined as PW.1 and also the Doctor as PW.2 and got marked the documents as per Exs.P1 to P19 in support of his case. On the contrary, respondent No.2 examined its Officer as RW.1 and produced two documents as Exs.R1 and R2. 4.4. On the basis of material evidence both oral and documentary, the tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.1,45,133/- with interest @ 6% p.a. 5. Being dissatisfied with the amount of compensation awarded by the tribunal, the claimant is before this Court in this appeal seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the tribunal.
texts.arguments: 6. It is the vehement contention of learned counsel for claimant that the tribunal has grossly erred in awarding meager compensation so also has erred in not taking into consideration the material evidence both oral and documentary, thereby causing miscarriage of justice to the claimant. It is further contended that the tribunal has erred in not awarding suitable compensation towards medical expenses based on records and has committed an error in awarding meager amount of 17,373/- which requires interference by this Court. He has also further contended that the tribunal has committed gross error in not awarding proper future loss of income due to disability suffered by the claimant and has not applied its mind in assessing the proper income of the claimant based on avocation and evidence on record. It is also contended by learned counsel that the tribunal has erred in not calculating the correct disability for assessing the loss of future earning capacity. On the basis of these submissions, he seeks to allow the appeal and consequently, seeks enhancement of compensation. 7. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent-Insurer vehemently contends that the judgment and award passed by the tribunal is in accordance with material evidence both oral and documentary and same does not call for any interference by this Court for the reason that the tribunal has considered the age and avocation and no material document produced with regard to proof of income and accordingly, notional income has been adopted by the tribunal, which does not call for interference by this Court. He also contends that the tribunal has awarded just and reasonable compensation under all other heads. Hence, no interference is called for in the present case as the appeal is devoid of merit and same deserved to be dismissed. On the basis of these submissions, he seeks for dismissal of the appeal and to affirm the judgment and award passed by the tribunal. Having heard the submissions of learned counsel for appellant-claimant and learned counsel for respondent- Insurer, the points that would arise for consideration are:- "(i) Whether the tribunal has awarded meager compensation and has committed an error in not considering the material evidence on record?
